rawFindings.title: Multiline single-token argument can make following arguments expected at column 0
rawFindings.explanation: This new condition also matches elements that start on the same line as the list opener but are a single token spanning multiple lines, such as a template literal. The code then bases the next element's indentation on that previous token's desired indentation. Since the previous token was on the opener line, its list offset was collapsed to the line indentation, so the next argument is expected at column 0 instead of one indent level.
rawFindings.suggestion: Only rebase on the previous element when its first token is on a later line than the list opener, or otherwise preserve the previous element's visual column when aligning the next element.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange:
With the default indent rule, `foo(`bar
baz`,
    qux
);` is now reported and autofixed to remove the 4-space indent before `qux`, even though continuation arguments should be indented one level.
